1261-program-description: A strong base in both, with core chemistry and honours physics and math. Graduate with CGPA 3.0 in program courses and overall. Specialized and demanding, with an adviser from each. 80 or 83 credits.
1262-complementary-courses-12-15-credits: At least 3 each of Chemistry and Physics. Without MATH 222, take it first term, making 83, and MATH 314 instead of MATH 248 if needed. 3 from a pair and 9 from the list. PHYS 459D1/D2 together.
1262-program-description: Enough of both for 400–500 level work, flexible toward either. Needs high standing in math, physics and computing. Graduate with CGPA 3.0 in program courses and overall. 78 or 81 credits. COMP 202 or equivalent is a prerequisite: Foundation course in U0, or first-term elective in U1.
1262-required-courses-63-credits: MATH 314 instead of MATH 248 in second term if scheduling requires.
1263-complementary-courses-15-credits: 6+ at 400–500 (not COMP 400 or PHYS 479), 3+ of those COMP. Without MATH 222, take it first term, making 81. 3–4, 6–7 and 3–4 from lists, including any 500-level PHYS or 400–500 COMP except COMP 400.
1263-program-description: Specialized and demanding, for graduate work and careers; optimized for theoretical physics, but good for experimental physics or math. Enter with high standing in CEGEP or Program Prerequisites. MATH 222, if needed, takes the first term without counting.
Below GPA 3.00 in a year, or below C in a course not fixed by supplemental or retake, means no continuing or graduating in Honours without both departments' permission. An adviser from each.
1264-u3-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3 from a pair, 6 from the list (PHYS 459D1/D2 together), and 3 of Honours Mathematics.
1266-about-physiology: Rooted in biology, chemistry, math and physics, overlapping other biomedical sciences and feeding clinical medicine. Studies molecules to systems in vertebrates: cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and renal, exercise, neurophysiology, endocrinology, immunology, biophysics and biomathematics, with links to many departments.
Careers in teaching, government and lab work, or medicine, dentistry and graduate study. All programs share a core, and U1 is identical except for the Joint programs, so you can decide later.

New students must contact the Student Affairs Officer for advising; returning students should check regularly, especially before final year. Complementary courses aren't electives: choose only from those listed (p. 36).
1266-interdepartmental-honours-in-immuno: See p. 1203. Contact Dr. Heather Melichar, Dr. Judith Mandl or Dr. Ana Nijnik.
1267-required-courses-33-credits: CEGEP CHEM 212 or 222 exempts you; take electives instead.
1267-upper-level-physiology-ulp-courses: 6 credits. PHGY 459D1/D2 counts as 3 ULP and 3 electives; PHGY 461D1/D2 as 3 ULP and 6 electives.
1268-program-description: Intensive physiology with related biomedical sciences. Enter in U2 after U1 requirements, with your adviser. 64–65 credits, with CHEM 212 on top if needed.
1268-complementary-courses-28-credits: 12–13 from four small lists, and 9 of Upper-Level Physiology (with PHGY 459D1/D2 and 461D1/D2 split between ULP and electives).

6 of Upper-Level Science. Chemistry, Neurology: all 300+ and listed ULS. Biochemistry, Computer Science, Microbiology and Immunology, Math, Physics, Pathology: all 300+. Anatomy, Biology, Experimental Medicine, Pharmacology, Psychology: listed ULS. ANAT 458 or BIOC 458. 3 of them may be replaced from a short list.
1270-program-description: Physiological systems and their math, from cells to behaviour, with pure and applied math, computing and problem-solving, especially nonlinear dynamics.
1271-program-description: Physics, math and physiology, applying physical methods to physiology and biology.
1272-program-description: Enter in U2 with U1 GPA 3.30 and at least B in PHGY 209 and 210. U3 needs U2 CGPA 3.20 and at least B in Physiology courses, with U2 standing weighing heavily. Numbers may be limited; otherwise transfer to the Major.

The listed deadline is August 23, 2019, likely out of date; forms are online or at McIntyre 1021. Contact Sonia Viselli. Graduate with CGPA 3.20 and at least B in all Physiology. CHEM 212 on top if needed.
1274-about-psychiatry: No B.Sc., but PSYT courses run through Science, for Arts, Science and graduate students, under their faculties' rules, including PSYT 400D1/D2.
1274-about-psychology: Programs in Arts (p. 391) and Science. The science of mind and behaviour, both social (culture, groups, relationships) and biological (neural basis, including other species).

Lab experiments and systematic observation seek general principles of perception, learning, motivation, cognition and social life, using measurement and statistics. It draws on biology, linguistics, sociology, philosophy and math. A young science, closing the gap between theory and fact.
1274-undergraduate-studies: Teaches core knowledge, theory and method, not applied training. A bachelor's isn't a professional qualification: Quebec's Order of Psychologists requires a doctorate, some undergraduate courses, and French. Useful also for medicine, education, social work, communication sciences and business. Honours adds research, high standards, and small groups with faculty.
1274-graduate-studies: A career needs graduate study, usually a Ph.D., for universities, institutes, hospitals, agencies, government, companies or consulting. Branches: social, cognitive, physiological, experimental, clinical, child, industrial, educational and more. Admission varies; both Major and Honours can qualify with high grades and sometimes research. Check requirements during U2.
1275-admission-requirements-for-the-bach: Apply through the Department; you hear by email before September. Honours: CGPA 3.00 and B in PSYC 380D1/D2 and 306, normally over U2 and U3; very strong students may join for U3 only. First Class: CGPA 3.50 and A- in those courses. See p. 1280.
1275-program-description: For B.Sc. students outside Psychology, with a separate version for Arts. 24 credits, at most 6 overlapping, C or better. PSYC 204 or equivalent first.
1275-program-prerequisite-0-3: PSYC 204 is recommended; with MATH 203 credit you can still take it for credit.
1276-program-description: A broad, less specialized overview with core and advanced courses, and optional research, leaving room for courses needed for graduate school and the Ordre des Psychologues du Québec.
1276-program-requirements: 45 credits, C minimum, plus a breadth component in a second area.
1276-required-course-12-credits: With a MATH 203 exemption: take PSYC 204 for credit, or go to PSYC 305 and add 3 credits of Psychology at 300+.
1278-program-description: In-depth core and advanced areas, optional research or related science, and room for courses needed for graduate school and the Ordre des Psychologues du Québec.
1278-program-prerequisites-0-6-credits: Introductory psychology and biology at college level, or in first year. CEGEP Introduction or General Psychology counts as PSYC 100; General Biology 1 or 2 is enough, otherwise BIOL 111 or 112.
1278-u1: With a MATH 203 exemption: take PSYC 204 for credit, or go to PSYC 305 and add 3 credits at 300+ in PSYC, ANAT, BIOC, BIOL, CHEM, COMP, MATH, PHGY or PSYT.
1279-list-b-social-health-and-developmen: 6 from List B, 9 of Psychology at 300+, 9 at 400–500, and 19 at 300+ in PSYC, ANAT, BIOL, BIOC, CHEM, COMP, MATH, PHGY or PSYT.
1279-unclassified-courses: Research and topics courses may also count.
1281-complementary-courses-30-credits: 3–9 from 500-level Psychology or the listed courses, with any rest at 400-level. U3 entrants may use PSYC 385, 484D1/D2 or 485. 21 of Honours courses.
1281-list-a: 6 credits from Behavioural Neuroscience, Cognition and Quantitative Methods. With COMP 202 or 204 and Foundation math, consider COMP 551; Psychology and CS students should prefer it over PSYC 560.
1282-list-b: 6 credits from Social, Health and Developmental. 9 at 300+ in ANAT, BIOC, BIOL, CHEM, COMP, MATH, PHGY, PSYT or PSYC.
1283-about-the-redpath-museum: Studies biological, geological and cultural diversity, with teaching, research and science education. Offers a Minor in Natural History. REDM courses count as Science.
1283-program-description: Exploring nature through specimens, objects and fieldwork, using museum collections. A required course at the Redpath and other McGill museums, breadth across zoology, botany, and earth and environmental sciences, and a compulsory field course.
1283-complementary-courses-21-credits: From Lists A (Zoology), B (Botany), C (Earth and Environmental Sciences) and D (Field). 3–9 each from A, B and C, 3+ from D, at most 3 at 200-level per list, and at most 9 outside Arts and Science.
1283-list-a-zoology: Introduction to Ecology and Evolution can go in A or B. ENTO 330 or BIOL 350.
1283-list-b-botany: Introduction to Ecology and Evolution can go in A or B.
1284-list-d-field-studies: Other field courses with the Adviser's permission.
1285-about-science-or-mathematics-for-te: Teacher certification comes through a B.Ed. under Quebec rules. This Minor lets you explore Education and earns some B.Ed. credits. Education also offers B.Ed. Secondary Science and Technology or Mathematics (p. 699), and the Master of Arts in Teaching and Learning.
1285-location: Dawson Hall, Room 405, 853 Sherbrooke St. W. Advisor: Gabrielle Ohayon, ISA Administrator.
1285-program-description: Explore Education without committing, earning some B.Ed. credits. B.Sc. graduates may also consider the MATL for a license. Limited, by application.
1285-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3, 3 and 6 from lists. EDES 335 or EDES 353.
1286-study-abroad-and-field-studies: Local, regional and international semesters, exchanges, internships and courses, often counting toward your major.
1286-opportunities-for-field-studies-and: Field Study Semesters and Off-Campus Courses (p. 1288): McGill courses elsewhere. Exchanges (p. 1289): at partners, paying McGill tuition. Independent Study Away (p. 1290): paying the host, earning McGill credit.
1286-internships-and-co-op-programs: See p. 65 or the Internship Offices Network.
1286-further-information-about-global-le: See the McGill Abroad site, or Student Exchanges through Service Point.
1286-field-study-semesters-and-off-campu: Packages of McGill courses for upper-years on physical and social environments: East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania), Canadian Arctic (Axel Heiberg Island), Barbados (two programs) and Panama. Limited; deadlines and costs vary, and courses may need prerequisites, so plan early. Any one can lead to the 18-credit Minor in Field Studies.
Off-campus courses, usually in summer and sometimes by separate application, in places like Italy, Mexico or Brazil, across arts, engineering, science, law and management.
1286-internship-and-field-studies-office: By appointment: 2001 McGill College, Room 646B. Minor Advisor: Curtis Sharman, SOUSA, Dawson Hall, 4th floor.
1286-program-overview: East Africa: 15 credits, 6 of context in natural and social sciences and 9 complementary. Winter term, 38 students. See p. 1194.
1287-fees: East Africa: on top of tuition, costs cover local travel, food, housing and park and museum fees, but not airfare, insurance or visas. See mcgill.ca/africa/program-fees.
1287-application-information: East Africa: apply online; deadlines usually in summer, perhaps a second intake in early September.
1287-prerequisites: East Africa: for your final two years.
1287-eligibility-for-external-students: East Africa: students elsewhere can apply if they qualify as McGill Visiting Students.
1287-program-overview: Arctic: 15 credits, 6 of background for an independent project and 9 complementary from ATOC, EPSC and Geography. Summer, Central Axel Heiberg Island, 10 students. See p. 1194.
1287-fees-2: Arctic: on top of fees, costs include airfare, travel, food, housing and other fees. See mcgill.ca/arctic/program-fees.
1287-prerequisites-2: Arctic: for your final two years; CGPA 3.00+ recommended.
1287-application-information-2: Arctic: online form, transcript, letter of intent, one reference, CV.
1287-program-overview-2: Barbados: 15 credits, 6 of context for a project and 9 complementary. Fall, Bellairs Research Institute, 15 students. See p. 1194.
1287-fees-3: Barbados: on top of tuition, costs include housing, most meals and field expenses, not airfare. See mcgill.ca/bfss/cost.
1287-application-information-3: Barbados: apply online in fall and winter for fall departure.
1288-program-overview: Barbados Interdisciplinary Tropical Studies, run by Agricultural and Environmental Sciences: class, lab and field trips, 15 credits. Summer, Bellairs Research Institute, 20 students. See p. 1194.
1288-fees: BITS: on top of fees, costs include housing, most meals and field expenses, not airfare. See mcgill.ca/bits/cost.
1288-application-information: BITS: email a letter of intent, CV, form and transcript to caroline.begg@mcgill.ca; see the site for deadlines.
1288-eligibility-for-international-stude: BITS: students elsewhere can apply if they qualify as McGill Visiting Students.
1288-program-overview-2: Panama: Winter, Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, 22 students. See p. 1194.
1288-fees-2: Panama: on top of tuition, costs include housing and field expenses, not airfare, food or living costs. See mcgill.ca/pfss/cost.
1288-application-information-2: Panama: apply online by May for the next winter; may be extended.
1288-prerequisites-2: Panama: HISP 218 and MATH 203 or equivalents required, CGPA 3.00+ recommended, for final-year students.
1288-architecture: Courses from the School of Architecture.
1289-biology: Biology courses from Science, including BIOL 334D1/D2.
1289-earth-and-planetary-sciences: Two-week May field studies in geoscience.
1289-history-and-classical-studies: Field courses from History and Classical Studies.
1289-desautels-faculty-of-management: Summer Abroad courses cover the same material as in Montreal, shaped by local business. See Minerva, or the BCom office at 514-398-4068.
1289-faculty-of-engineering: FACC 501, normally in Winter, includes the "Israel Start-Up Nation" study trip the following August, open across McGill.
1289-exchange-programs: A term or year at a partner, earning McGill credit and paying McGill tuition (billed as 15 credits a term). Over 150 universities in 39 countries; spaces vary, and some are faculty-specific.
1289-eligibility: All nationalities. Be full-time and degree-seeking, meet your faculty's criteria, and have a full year (24 McGill credits) by the start. One or two terms.
1289-applying-to-go-on-exchange: In Minerva. Fall and full-year: December to mid-January. Winter dates to be confirmed. Law has its own deadlines.
1290-exchanges-within-quebec: Through BCI's Inter-University Transfer Agreement, take courses at any Quebec university for home credit.
1290-transfer-of-credits-from-host-insti: Host grades aren't on your transcript or in your CGPA; it shows the exchange, transfer credits and exemptions. Start once registered, with syllabi, and finish soon after. Send an official transcript to officialschooldocs@mcgill.ca.
1290-independent-study-away: Apply and pay the host directly as a visiting student, for places without exchanges. Ask your faculty's Student Affairs Office and the host's admissions.
1290-funding-opportunities-for-going-abr: Awards and aid exist; see below and McGill Abroad.
1290-government-student-financial-assist: On exchange you're full-time, so Canadians can apply for government aid, and Americans for Title IV loans within limits (ask Student Aid). On Independent Study Away, no aid through McGill; check with the host.
1290-scholarships-and-awards: Renewable awards may continue for a year if you're full-time elsewhere. Annual in-course awards use only McGill grades, so exchange students miss them the next year.
1290-mobility-bursaries-for-exchanges: Quebec's PMICSE funds need-based help for undergraduates approved for an eligible exchange, through Student Aid.
1290-enriched-educational-opportunities-: Need-based help for field semesters, field courses, and unpaid off-campus internships and research, through Student Aid.
1287-funding-2: Barbados: you can apply for the need-based Enriched Educational Opportunities bursary (EEO). See mcgill.ca/studentaid/special-funding/eeo.
1288-funding: Barbados Interdisciplinary Tropical Studies: you can apply for the need-based Enriched Educational Opportunities bursary (EEO). See mcgill.ca/studentaid/special-funding/eeo.
1287-funding: East Africa: you can apply for the need-based Enriched Educational Opportunities bursary (EEO). See mcgill.ca/studentaid/special-funding/eeo.
